definition: A non-native speech database is a speech database of non-native pronunciations of English.
details: Such databases are used in the development of: multilingual automatic speech recognition systems, text to speech systems, pronunciation trainers, and second language learning systems.

explainer.lead: A non-native speech database collects English pronunciations from people for whom English is not their native language. It provides speech material for building recognizers, speech synthesizers, pronunciation trainers, and language-learning systems.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a library filled with recordings of people learning to speak English. Engineers can listen to and study these recordings to make computers better at understanding speech or helping people practise pronunciation.
tiers.practitioner: Use this kind of database when developing multilingual speech recognition, text-to-speech, pronunciation-training, or second-language-learning systems. It supplies non-native English speech rather than a standard performance score, so its role and usefulness depend on the system being developed.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, a non-native speech database is a speech database D containing non-native pronunciations of English. D is used in the development of multilingual automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, pronunciation-training, and second-language-learning systems; no scoring function is inherent in the definition.

explainer.example: A non-native speaker's recording of an English sentence is added to the database. A development team can then use that recording while building a multilingual speech recognizer or a pronunciation trainer.

usedIn.name: Multilingual automatic speech recognition
usedIn.detail: Provides non-native English speech for developing recognition systems.

usedIn.name: Text-to-speech systems
usedIn.detail: Supplies speech material for speech-synthesis development.

usedIn.name: Pronunciation trainers
usedIn.detail: Provides examples of non-native pronunciation for training-tool development.

usedIn.name: Second-language learning
usedIn.detail: Supports systems designed to help people learn another language.

explainer.measures: It does not measure a single quantity or assign a standard score; it collects non-native pronunciations of English as speech data.
howScored: No standard scoring procedure is defined.
The database provides speech material rather than benchmark results.
caveats: The term describes a kind of database, not one named corpus.
It does not define a metric, leaderboard, or typical numerical result.
